title: What is an Agent?
description: Loops, tools, decisions. Understand the building blocks of autonomous systems.

title: Think → Act → Observe
description: The agent loop. How agents reason and take action.

title: Tool Use Patterns
description: Function calling, chaining, composition. How agents use tools to solve problems.

title: State & Memory
description: Keep context across turns. Store what the agent learns.

title: Guardrails & Human-in-the-Loop
description: Deciding what an agent should never do alone, and where to add a checkpoint.

title: What an Agent Actually Is
description: The four things that turn a single model call into an agent — a loop, tools, a stopping condition, and a boundary between what the model decides and what your code decides — and the honest cases where an agent is either the obvious right shape or a mistake dressed up as one.

title: Tools
description: How to define a tool so the model calls it correctly on the first attempt: a description written for a reader who can't see your code, a schema that makes the wrong argument hard to construct, return values the model can actually act on, and the point where adding more tools makes the agent worse at picking any of them.

title: Controlling the Loop
description: Deciding, in code, when an agent keeps going, stops, or hands control to a human — enforced stopping conditions, step/time/cost limits, detecting a loop that's spinning without progress, when to interrupt for a human decision, and how to resume a run that stopped partway through without losing its place.

title: Errors Inside the Loop
description: What actually happens in the model's head — mechanically, not metaphorically — when a tool call errors, why a bad error message produces a confidently wrong next step, how to decide between retrying, changing approach, and stopping, the specific failure of an agent reporting success after something silently failed, and how to make a failure loud instead of quietly wrong.
